svg.text: Putting PPE on and taking it off — the order is the safety
DONNING — putting on
1 Hand hygiene
2 GOWN
3 MASK or respirator — fit check it
4 EYE protection — goggles or visor
5 GLOVES — last, over the gown cuff
DOFFING — taking off
1 GLOVES — dirtiest, so they go first
2 Hand hygiene
3 GOWN — roll it away from you
4 EYE protection, then MASK — by the ties
5 Hand hygiene again
The logic, so you never have to memorise the list
Put on in the order of how long it must stay clean. Take off in the order of how contaminated it is.
Gloves go on LAST and come off FIRST. The mask stays on longest — it comes off outside the room,
and it is always removed by the ties or elastic, never by touching the front.
Gloves — the four errors that spread infection rather than prevent it
Wearing one pair between two patients · Washing gloves instead of changing them
Touching the notes, the phone or a door handle with gloves on · Skipping hand hygiene after removal
Gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene. Hands are contaminated during removal, and gloves leak.
